extracted.intended_audience: USPTO employees (especially patent examiners and supervisors) and practitioners interacting with the Office
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural standards from MPEP Chapter 1700 governing (1) examiner and USPTO employee communications and testimony regarding patents, (2) post-employment restrictions, (3) Official Gazette content/access, (4) application recordation and examiner time/activity/docket rules, and (5) dissemination and treatment of court/PTAB decisions and information resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office personnel not to express opinion on validity, patentability, expiration, or enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: Every employee of the USPTO shall refuse to express to any person any opinion as to the validity or invalidity of, or the patentability or unpatentability of any claim in any U.S. patent or the expiration date of any patent, except to the extent necessary to carry out specified Office functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions (A–H) where opinions/determinations may be given: (A) examination of a non-reissue patent application where expiration date necessary for examination; (B) examination of a reissue application of the patent; (C) supplemental examination or reexamination proceedings; (D) interference or derivation proceeding involving the patent; (E) patent term adjustment/extension under 35 U.S.C. 154/156 where determination of expiration date necessary; (F) notification that a patent has expired for failure to pay maintenance fee; (G) consideration of a request under the regulations (e.g., a petition) where patent term determination is necessary or ancillary; (H) inter partes or post-grant review. Employees may provide general factual information about patent term calculation (e.g., design patent term rules) but should refuse to determine or opine on a specific patent's expiration date except as provided above. Employees must refuse inquiries that could indicate a patent should not have issued; accepting private payments (bounties) for prior-art searching or accepting payments from outside sources for prior art search activities may lead to disciplinary action. Examiners should not suggest a field of search if the invention has been patented. Employees who examined an application should not discuss whether a particular reference was considered or whether a claim would have been allowed over that reference; the file must speak for itself. Definitions in 37 CFR 104.1 and exceptions in 37 CFR 104.21 apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office personnel not to testify (general prohibition and notification obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO policy is that employees, including patent examiners, will not appear as witnesses or give testimony in legal proceedings except under conditions specified in 37 CFR Part 104, Subpart C. Any employee who testifies contrary to this policy may be dismissed or removed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asked to testify or upon receipt of a subpoena, the employee must immediately notify the Office of the USPTO General Counsel. Requests for testimony should be referred immediately to that Office. Any individual desiring testimony of an employee must comply with 37 CFR Part 104, Subpart C. Requests for deposition testimony of an examiner in a pending ex parte reexamination will generally be denied due to the ex parte nature of the proceeding. A request for testimony should be made to the Office of the General Counsel at least ten (10) working days prior to the expected testimony date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and limits of permissible testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: If an employee is authorized to testify, testimony is limited to facts within the employee's personal knowledge; employees are prohibited from giving expert or opinion testimony or answering hypothetical or speculative questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees are forbidden to testify as experts or to express opinions as to validity. They may not answer hypothetical/speculative questions or questions probing mental processes, analyses, or conclusions. Case law cited (e.g., Fischer & Porter Co. v. Corning Glass Works; In re Mayewsky; Shaffer Tool Works v. Joy Mfg. Co.) supports limiting testimony to relevant matters of fact and avoiding exploration of mental processes or basis for examiner decisions. Testimony will not be permitted on privileged subject matter. If authorized, the Office will determine impermissible topics and will preclude responses accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impermissible questions when an employee testifies
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions attempting to discover mental processes, expertise, qualifications, or internal deliberations of a quasi-judicial employee are impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of impermissible questions include inquiries into: (A) employee's background, expertise, qualifications to examine a particular matter, usual practice or whether the employee followed MPEP/TMEP/manual procedures in a particular case, consultations with other Office employees, understanding of inventions/prior art/Office manuals/regulations/laws/responsibilities of other employees, or reliance on particular facts or arguments; (B) the manner and extent to which the employee considered or studied material in performing a quasi-judicial function; (C) the bases, reasons, mental processes, analyses, or conclusions of the employee in performing the quasi-judicial function. The Office will determine and bar impermissible questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for requests to obtain testimony or depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for testimony must comply with 37 CFR 104.22(c); in some circumstances a subpoena may be obviated if the requesting party meets further Office-specified conditions (A–E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions to avoid necessity of subpoena: (A) identify the civil action (style, action number, district, judge, and counsel contact info); (B) agree not to ask questions precluded by 37 CFR 104.23; (C) comply with applicable Federal Rules of Civil Procedure (e.g., Rule 30) and give ten (10) working days' notice (fifteen (15) working days if deposition desired between Nov 15 and Jan 15); (D) notice the deposition at a place convenient to the USPTO (Office of General Counsel conference room is deemed convenient); (E) supply the USPTO a copy of the deposition transcript for its records. Absent meeting A–E, a party must comply with the precise terms of 37 CFR 104.22(c) and a subpoena will be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on current and former Office employees regarding patents (35 U.S.C. 4 and 37 CFR 11.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers and employees of the USPTO may not apply for a patent or acquire any patent or interest in a patent during their appointment and for one year thereafter; post-employment practice before the Office is restricted under 37 CFR 11.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 4 bars applying for patents or acquiring rights during employment and for one year after; any patents applied for thereafter cannot claim priority earlier than one year after termination. 37 CFR 11.10 requires post-employment undertakings by former Office employees: they must agree not to knowingly act as agent/attorney for others before the Office in connection with any patent or application they participated in personally and substantially as an Office employee, and not to act within two years after termination as agent/attorney before the Office in connection with any particular patent/application if such matter was pending under their official responsibility within one year prior to termination. By virtue of conflict-of-interest statutes (e.g., 18 U.S.C. 203, 205) and OGE regulations, former employees remain barred from prosecuting or aiding prosecution of patent/trademark applications where conflicts exist. An Office employee named as inventor will be presumed incapable of executing an inventor's oath/declaration under 35 U.S.C. 4; for applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 may be filed in lieu of the employee's oath/declaration without contacting the current employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette publication content and browsing features
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette (OG) is published electronically weekly in two sections (Patents and Trademarks) and provides listings and browsing functionality for issued patents and trademarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Electronic Official Gazette — Patents (eOG:P) reports reexamination certificates, reissues, plant, utility, and design patents issued and statutory invention registrations. Browse features: (A) Browse by CPC or USPC to access patents by classification; (B) Classification of Patents page linking to patents within CPC classes and USPC class ranges; (C) Browse Granted Patents page to access patents by number or type and links to certificates from reexaminations/supplemental examinations/administrative trials; (D) Index of Patentees (alphabetical/cumulative); (E) Geographical Index of Inventors; (F) Notices page linking to weekly USPTO Notices. For each patent the OG may provide: (A) patent number; (B) title of invention; (C) inventor(s) name, city, state/country; (D) assignee info; (E) applicant info; (F) filing date and application number; (G) reissue cross-reference; (H) U.S. benefit application data; (I) PCT/international design application data; (J) foreign priority data; (K) publication number and date; (L) international classification; (M) CPC classification; (N) U.S. class/subclass (for design/plant); (O) number of claims; (P) selected drawing figure; (Q) a claim or claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette Notices and types of notices published
rubrics_metrics.description: Official Gazette Notices publish regular and special notices relevant to patents and trademarks and include certain administrative and public notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices include: patent and trademark suits, disclaimers filed, Certificates of Correction issued, lists of applications and patents available for license or sale, notices of 37 CFR 1.47 applications, general information (orders, notices, rule changes, changes in classification), certain adverse interference decisions, condition of work in the Office, registration of attorneys/agents, reprimands, suspensions, exclusions of registered practitioners, and notices to parties not reached by mail. OG Notices are available on the USPTO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated application records and integrated examination tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO maintains an automated data management system and integrated examination tools for retrieval and online updating of patent application records, examiner time/activity, docketing and technical support backlog records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactions into the automated system are entered by keyed entries or drop-down selections. Retrievable/updatable items include classification, examiner docket, attorney, inventor, status, prosecution history, and paper application location. The IFW (Image File Wrapper) system scans paper components into electronic images and, for IFW files, the IFW is the official file. Non-patent literature access differs. Patent Center and Private PAIR are the primary status/info systems; Private PAIR requires Customer Number for unpublished apps. See MPEP § 2701, § 403, and related sections for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biweekly time and activity reporting requirement for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must report examining and non-examining time on a biweekly basis; these entries are used to compute productivity and produce time and activity reports accessible via integrated examination tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners can view biweekly reports showing applications for which actions have been counted and the type of action counted. Reports also show time data, action summaries, and cumulative summaries for the quarter and fiscal year. Examiners should check reports to verify all worked-on applications are properly listed. Missing or incorrect information should be promptly reported to the SPE or TC troubleshooter for correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner docket maintenance, FAOM counting, and 'disposals' rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner dockets are maintained in the automated system and include new/amended dockets, rejected application dockets, and lists of regular/special/expedited applications. Counting rules determine First Action on the Merits (FAOM) credits and 'disposal' credits for performance reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First Action on the Merits (FAOM): the first time an examiner performs a merit action (rejection final/non-final, Ex parte Quayle, allowance) credit is received for FAOM. A second/subsequent FAOM may occur when the first action was a mailed restriction/election and the second is a merits action; the system automatically determines FAOM. Disposals (examiner credit) include: (A) Allowance; (B) Abandonment; (C) Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs); (D) Examiner's Answer; (E) International Preliminary Examination Report; (F) Institution of an interference or derivation proceeding where application would be in condition for allowance but for the proceeding. Office-level disposals consist only of allowances and abandonments. No disposal credit is received for allowance or abandonment after an Examiner's Answer or a decision by a court or the PTAB, though such actions are reflected on the time and activity report. Correction process: missing/incorrect info on reports should be reported to SPE/TC troubleshooter for updates; final-year corrections should be reported immediately to SPE to ensure accurate fiscal-year records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination of court and Patent Trial and Appeal Board decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for forwarding and circulating precedential court and PTAB opinions within the USPTO to inform examiners and supervisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of the Solicitor forwards precedential court decisions to the Office of the Commissioner for Patents, who forwards to TC Directors, Office of Patent Training, and Director of Office of Patent Quality Assurance. TC Directors should make copies available to supervisors and other appropriate individuals and are encouraged to discuss contents in staff meetings to reinforce examination quality. PTAB decisions are returned to the examiner, who takes action consistent with the decision unless rehearing is requested; TC Directors may circulate/discuss PTAB decisions among supervisors and examiners depending on subject matter or issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of court and PTAB decisions that affect USPTO policy and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Board or court decision significantly changes law or provides new interpretations affecting USPTO policy/practice, the USPTO follows a defined process to evaluate, draft guidance, and incorporate policy updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an examiner or supervisor concludes a decision affects policy/practice, the matter should be raised to the appropriate TC Director via normal chain-of-command. The TC Director consults the Deputy Commissioner for Patents who oversees the Office of Petitions and provides a draft recommended guidance. The Deputy Commissioner consults appropriate Office officials and recommends to the Commissioner for Patents. Senior officials (Director, General Counsel, Solicitor, Chief APJ, Commissioner for Patents, Deputy Commissioners, TC Director) may meet to review policy ramifications. Communications of determinations typically occur via Official Gazette and/or memorandum to USPTO personnel. Policy implications are officially incorporated into the MPEP and Office of Patent Training curriculum during the next update cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information sources and customer assistance resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact points, databases, and tools available to the public and examiners for patent information, filing, and assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key resources: USPTO Contact Center (800-PTO-9199; 571-272-1000), Inventors Assistance Center, Public Search Facilities (addresses and hours listed), Patent Electronic Business Center (EBC) for electronic filing and Private PAIR assistance (866-217-9197), Patent Grants Database (full-text since 1976), Patent Applications Database (published apps since March 15, 2001), Patent Center and Private PAIR (status info; Customer Number for Private PAIR access), Image File Wrapper (IFW) system (IFW is official file for scanned apps), Assignments on the Web (AOTW) for recorded assignments, Global Dossier Public Access and WIPO-CASE for family and citation data (includes Office action indicators and machine translations). Certified Copy Center (CCC) Storefront (MyUSPTO account required) for ordering copies. PatentIn software support via EBC. Office of Petitions handles petitions (contact details and ePetition options provided). Various phone numbers, email contacts, and web links are provided in the MPEP for each resource.
